title: Stuffed Pepper Soup
tagline: Every part of a stuffed pepper, none of the stuffing.
description: Ground sirloin, green pepper, tomatoes and rice in one pot: the stuffed-pepper flavor in about an hour, with no hollowing, stuffing or baking. Thyme and sage do the seasoning.
ingredients: 1 can (29 oz / 822g) diced tomatoes, with juice
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a large pot or deep skillet over medium-high. Add the beef and break it up as it cooks, 5-7 minutes, until browned and crumbly with no pink left. Spoon off the fat.
Add the green pepper and onion. Cook, stirring, about 5 minutes, until the onion is soft and translucent.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, broth, thyme and sage, and season with salt and pepper. Cover and simmer 30-45 minutes, until the peppers are tender.
While it simmers, bring the water and rice to a boil in a saucepan. Cover, drop to medium-low and cook 20-25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Stir the rice into the soup, heat through, taste for salt and pepper, and serve.
notes: Leftovers: the rice keeps drinking broth in the fridge, so day-two soup gets thick. Thin it with broth or water when reheating, or store the rice separately and stir it in per bowl.
Freezes well without the rice, up to 3 months. Cook fresh rice when you reheat.
Ground sirloin is lean, so there's little fat to drain. With 80/20 beef, drain well before the vegetables go in.
Shredded cheddar or mozzarella on top is the stuffed-pepper move.
troubleshooting: Tastes flat → under-salted; canned tomatoes and broth vary, so taste and salt at the end, not just the start.
Peppers still crunchy → simmered too short; give it the full 45 minutes and check a piece.
Greasy surface → fat not drained after browning; skim with a wide spoon.
Thick and stodgy leftovers → the rice absorbed the broth; thin with liquid when reheating.
